visuals.heading: It You, Your Manager, or the Company

items.text: A skilled person with a strong manager can grow inside a flat company.
It is not a complaint session and not an exit interview.

blocks.heading: Layer 3 Checks Out, Real Roles

items.text: Career growth is now a top-tier retention factor for employees in India specifically, which is why more mid-size and large employers have formalised internal job boards, mentorship-linked mobility programs, and cross-functional project rotations over the last few years, not as a favour, but because replacing and onboarding external hires costs more than moving someone who already knows the systems and culture.
Before you apply, name the specific new capability the move would force you to build.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The 3-Layer Plateau Check: is it you, your manager, or the company?

rows: Pick one new skill or piece of scope, build it deliberately, produce visible proof of it
A concrete new capability you can point to in a review or interview, not just busyness
A direct conversation naming what you want, followed by a skip-level if nothing moves after one cycle
Your manager can name a specific room, meeting, or person they raised your case with
Apply for a genuine internal lateral move, or start an honest external search while employed
Real, open internal postings above your level exist and are actually being filled

visuals.heading: Skip-Level Conversation That Actually Moves Something

blocks.heading: Step 1 Set Up

items.text: Step 1, Set up the meeting through the normal channel.
Step 2, Bring one clear ask, not a list of grievances.
Step 3, Let them talk more than you do.
Step 4, Follow up in writing within a few days.
Step 5, Give it one full review cycle, then reassess.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: How to run a skip-level conversation that actually moves something

blocks.heading: Using an External Offer As Advantage

items.text: Get the market read even if you are not sure you want to leave.
Bring the offer to your manager as information, not an ultimatum.
Be genuinely willing to take the offer.
Watch for a counter-offer that fixes pay but not scope.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Using an external offer as advantage, without actually needing to leave

blocks.heading: Out Longer Than It Needs to Be

items.text: Assuming it's the company before checking Layer 1 and 2.
Assuming it's you when it's actually the company.
Quiet quitting instead of diagnosing.
Treating a skip-level as a one-time fix.

Waiting indefinitely for "next year." If the same promise has repeated across two review cycles with no concrete milestone attached, that pattern is itself the answer to the structural-layer question.
